title: HTOPS shows age-structured social support, participation, and domain-specific authority
source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Household Trends and Outlook Pulse Survey, topical 2607

denominator.unit: estimated U.S. population age 18 and older represented in published HTOPS tables

social_emotional_support_always_or_usual.unit: percent of adults who always or usually obtain social and emotional support

social_emotional_support_never.unit: percent of adults who never obtain social and emotional support

religious_services_12_or_more_times.unit: percent attending religious services 12 or more times in the past 12 months

clubs_or_organizations_12_or_more_times.unit: percent attending club or organization meetings 12 or more times in the past 12 months

doctor_health_information_trust_great_de.unit: percent reporting a great deal or quite a lot of trust in health information from doctors

ai_health_information_trust_great_deal_o.unit: percent reporting a great deal or quite a lot of trust in health information from AI tools

live_music_dance_theater_attendance.unit: percent attending a live music, dance, or theater performance in the past four weeks

movie_attendance.unit: percent going to the movies in the past four weeks

observations.method: Descriptive calculations from published HTOPS population-count columns. Each percentage is the relevant response count divided by the total population estimate for the same row and rounded to one decimal place.
observations.uncertainty: The Census Bureau labels the HTOPS estimates experimental and warns that estimates for subpopulations may have small sample sizes and large standard errors. Standard-error workbooks were downloaded for all four tables but no inferential age comparison is claimed here.
observations.subgroup: Age groups 18–34, 35–49, 50–64, and 65 and above; additional published characteristics are available in the workbooks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Age gradients may reflect cohort, health, retirement, time availability, survey response, or question-specific participation differences rather than a single change in social connectedness. The AI and doctor trust measures are domain-specific and should not be treated as general institutional trust. Cross-sectional values do not show change over time or causal effects.

boundary: This record establishes a current descriptive social/cultural surface and an age-differentiated authority comparison. It does not establish a time trend, causal age effect, general institutional legitimacy, political behavior, or one respondent-level chain from social support to action.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Census release page, four official XLSX detailed tables, and four corresponding standard-error workbooks reviewed; source workbooks are not committed to the repository.
